scope: Bounded control/MOV DR source gates23–24, deterministic glibc input preparation, and completed musl probe6 that powers off without a guest receipt. No workload or release qualification.
limitations: P02 remains incomplete. No physical x86 receipt, full ISA/debug/control qualification, complete userspace workload receipt, glibc boot, systemd, sustained stress or release qualification is established.

Run23 remains a failed incremental gate:694 actual Swift passes,5 failing methods,16 issues and1 disabled physical-reference method. Identical source passes clean24 with699 actual Swift passes plus1 disabled; both XCTest runs pass10 and skip1 optional fixture.
Probe6 runs the copied run22 executable, not the run24 source. It observes ACPI S5/powered-off but misses the required guest receipt and exits1; only D is visible from userspace.

Glibc evidence proves pinned ELF dependency closure and deterministic archive preparation only. All seven intended workloads use glibc BusyBox; only the final shutdown helper uses separately pinned klibc. No guest binary executes during preparation.
The ARM64 macOS27 beta/Xcode17F109/SDK26.5 host remains experimental. Compiler release optimization and successful schema validation are not release qualification.
Generated FFI input identities and runner executable hashes are retained without vendoring binary payloads. Glibc fixture binaries remain reproducible external inputs.

The MOV DR overlapping-fault order is a narrow Dory compatibility policy based on externally reported Intel observations; AMD differs for GD versus CPL. This is separate from local physical-reference qualification and adds no breakpoint/watchpoint engine.

No CPU capability bits are promoted. Broader control/descriptor semantics, alignment checks, breakpoint execution, optional instruction gates, syscall/stress coverage and complete phase acceptance remain open.
UART run25 and later guest probes are deliberately excluded from this through-run24 receipt.
